moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
learningObjectives: Use Blueprint to incorporate best practices and decades of Pega expertise through available templates.
Import a Blueprint into Pega Platform to build an application.

elements.description: A generative-AI-infused tool that changes how teams envision digital transformation. It enables rapid, collaborative application design through workflow design, helping teams align on an optimized solution and get into development far faster than the weeks-to-months traditional design once took.

Blueprint operates INDEPENDENTLY as a SaaS tool, separate from existing Pega Studios — no Pega instance or login is required to collaborate (stakeholders with a Pega login can still participate). You create a Blueprint at pega.com/blueprint.

Blueprint does NOT replace App Studio or other Pega tools; it augments them by offering a fresh, collaborative way to transform ideas into a functional application in record time, incorporating decades of Pega best practices through templates.

elements.text: Blueprint is the architect's collaborative whiteboard: the whole team sketches the building together before any concrete is poured, using proven blueprints (best-practice templates), then hands the finished drawing to the construction crew (Pega Platform).

bulletPoints: Blueprint delivers detailed best-practice application templates instantly, embedding decades of Pega expertise.
Goal: align the team on an optimal design and reach development faster than ever.

elements.description: You describe what you are trying to build in business terms; Blueprint uses that information to PROPOSE Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas — enabling quick design edits to fit business requirements.

After the initial AI-proposed design, you refine it collaboratively — adding/editing Stages, Processes, Steps, fields, data objects, and Personas — so the Blueprint matches the desired workflow before importing.
Blueprint offers powerful, detailed best-practice application templates instantly, helping teams incorporate Pega's accumulated expertise rather than starting from a blank canvas.

elements.text: Generating a Blueprint is like giving a skilled drafter a paragraph about your business: they hand back a labeled floor plan (Case Types, Life Cycles, Data Model, Personas) that you then mark up together until it's right.

bulletPoints: Blueprint proposes the full app skeleton: Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas.
Collaboration needs no Pega login, so business stakeholders can co-design directly.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Importing a Pega Blueprint into Pega Platform

elements.description: You export the resulting Blueprint and import the file directly into Pega Platform (a new or existing application), jumpstarting a demo or project build-out by producing a functional application in minutes.

The Lead System Architect (LSA) is responsible for importing the Blueprint file into the Pega Platform environment and uses the user stories created by Blueprint and BAs to configure functional and technical requirements.
On import, Pega creates the Blueprint's assets according to your configuration. ALL the assets are created in a Branch EXCEPT Access Roles.
Pega GenAI PremBridge is NOT required to import Pega Blueprints into a new or existing application.

elements.text: Importing a Blueprint is like importing a fully-furnished room layout into your house plan: everything drops into a staging area (a Branch) for review — except the keys (Access Roles), which are handled separately.

bulletPoints: Import jumpstarts development: a functional application appears in minutes.
Branch on import holds all assets EXCEPT Access Roles; the LSA performs the import.
PremBridge is not a prerequisite for importing a Blueprint.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Using Blueprint for an Industry App (Customer Service for Insurance)

elements.description: Blueprint can be used to create industry-specific applications — for example, a Customer Service for Insurance application — by starting from relevant best-practice templates and refining the proposed Case Types and workflows for the industry's needs.

elements.text: Industry templates are pre-fab housing kits: instead of designing an insurance service app from scratch, you start from a kit tuned for that industry and customize the rooms (Case Types/workflows).

bulletPoints: Starting from an industry template accelerates design while keeping Pega best practices.
The team refines the proposed design to fit the specific organization before importing into Pega Platform.

examPitfalls.title: Blueprint is standalone SaaS — no login to collaborate
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Tests imply Blueprint runs inside a Pega instance or requires everyone to log in. It is independent SaaS; collaboration needs no Pega login.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Remember Blueprint is separate from the Studios; stakeholders can co-design without a Pega login.

examPitfalls.title: Blueprint augments, not replaces, App Studio
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Distractors claim Blueprint replaces App Studio/Dev Studio.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Blueprint augments existing tools by accelerating design; you still build/refine in App Studio.

examPitfalls.title: What Blueprint proposes
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The proposal set is tested: Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Blueprint drafts the app skeleton (workflow + data + personas), not infrastructure or production integrations.

examPitfalls.title: Who imports the Blueprint
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Import is performed by the Lead System Architect (LSA), not the BA or a generic role.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: BAs/Blueprint create user stories; the LSA imports the Blueprint and configures from those stories.

examPitfalls.title: Import creates assets in a Branch EXCEPT Access Roles
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A precise fact frequently tested: every asset lands in a Branch except Access Roles.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: If asked which asset is NOT created in the Branch on import, the answer is Access Roles.

examPitfalls.title: PremBridge is not required to import
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates assume PremBridge is a prerequisite for Blueprint import.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Pega GenAI PremBridge is NOT required to import a Blueprint into a new or existing application.

examPitfalls.title: Import target can be new OR existing
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Some think Blueprint only creates brand-new applications.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A Blueprint can be imported into a new application or an existing one to jumpstart the build.

examPitfalls.title: Best-practice templates value
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The exam stresses that Blueprint embeds decades of Pega expertise via templates.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Blueprint's templates instantly apply Pega best practices, including for industry apps like Customer Service for Insurance.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A business team without Pega logins wants to collaboratively design a new application before any development begins. What makes Pega Blueprint suitable?

options.text: It is a standalone SaaS tool that requires no Pega instance or login to collaborate
It runs only inside Dev Studio
It requires every participant to have an LSA license
It can only be used after the app is already built

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint is a standalone SaaS tool requiring no Pega Platform login to collaborate.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint operates independently as SaaS and needs no Pega instance or login to collaborate (those with a login can still join). The other options contradict this.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After you describe an application in business terms, what does Blueprint propose?

options.text: Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas
Server hardware and network topology
Only a list of Rulesets
Only Access Roles

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint uses AI to draft the application skeleton — Case Types, Data Models, and Personas.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint proposes Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas, which you then refine. It does not propose infrastructure or only Rulesets/Access Roles.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A project manager asks whether importing a Pega Blueprint means the team no longer needs App Studio for ongoing development. Which statement about Blueprint's relationship to App Studio is correct?

options.text: Blueprint augments App Studio and other Pega tools; it does not replace them
Blueprint replaces App Studio entirely
Blueprint is a feature inside Admin Studio
Blueprint and App Studio cannot be used on the same project

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint augments App Studio without replacing it; the two tools work together in sequence.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint augments existing Pega tools by accelerating design; you still build and refine in App Studio. It is not a replacement and is not part of Admin Studio.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Who is responsible for importing the Blueprint file into the Pega Platform environment?

options.text: The Lead System Architect (LSA)
The Product Owner
The Scrum Master
The end customer

practiceQuiz.hint: The most senior member of the System Architect family imports the Blueprint into Pega Platform.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The LSA imports the Blueprint file and configures functional and technical requirements from the user stories. The PO manages scope and priorities; the BA authors user stories; the Scrum Master facilitates ceremonies.

practiceQuiz.scenario: When a Blueprint is imported, the system creates the assets in a Branch. Which asset is the EXCEPTION not created in the Branch?

options.text: Access Roles
Case Types
Data objects
Personas

practiceQuiz.hint: One specific asset type is NOT placed in the Branch during a Blueprint import — it relates to security.
practiceQuiz.rationale: On Blueprint import, all assets are created in a Branch EXCEPT Access Roles. Case Types, data objects, and Personas are all created within the Branch for review before merging.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team believes they must install Pega GenAI PremBridge before they can import a Blueprint. Is this correct?

options.text: No — PremBridge is not required to import a Blueprint into a new or existing application
Yes — PremBridge is mandatory for all imports
Yes — but only for existing applications
No — but the Blueprint cannot target an existing application

practiceQuiz.hint: PremBridge is NOT a prerequisite; Blueprint imports can target a new or an existing application.
practiceQuiz.rationale: PremBridge is NOT required to import Blueprints. A Blueprint can be imported into a new or an existing application, and no additional license bridge is needed for the import step.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the primary value of importing a Blueprint into Pega Platform?

options.text: It jumpstarts a demo or project by producing a functional application in minutes
It permanently locks the application to Blueprint
It deletes existing Case Types
It disables App Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: Importing a Blueprint produces a functional, demonstrable application in a matter of minutes.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Importing a Blueprint produces a functional application in minutes, jumpstarting demos and development build-outs. The application is not production-ready immediately, and the import does not take days or require manual schema setup.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA team is about to generate their first Blueprint for a claims application and wants to understand the process. Which TWO statements correctly describe how generating and modifying a Blueprint works?

options.text: You describe the app in business terms and Blueprint proposes an initial design
You refine the proposal (Stages, Steps, fields, data objects, Personas) before importing
Once generated, a Blueprint cannot be edited
Generation requires writing Java code

practiceQuiz.hint: The Blueprint workflow follows: describe → AI proposes → team refines → export/import into Pega.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint proposes an initial design from a business-terms description, and you refine it collaboratively before import. Blueprints are editable and require no Java. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team wants to stand up a Customer Service for Insurance application quickly while following Pega best practices. How does Blueprint help?

options.text: It provides industry best-practice templates to start from, which the team refines for their needs
It forbids any customization of the generated design
It only works for generic, non-industry apps
It requires rebuilding all Case Types by hand first

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint includes industry-specific templates to accelerate design for common business domains.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint offers best-practice and industry-specific templates to accelerate design; teams refine the AI proposal before importing it. Blueprint supports customization and industry scenarios, not just generic processes.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why did Pega create Blueprint, given that traditional application design took weeks to months?

options.text: Its GenAI-infused approach helps teams align on an optimized solution and reach development faster
To remove the need for any business stakeholder input
To replace the Case Life Cycle concept
To store production data

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint speeds stakeholder alignment during design, reducing time before development can begin.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint's generative-AI approach helps teams align on an optimized design and get into development faster than the slow traditional process. It increases (not removes) stakeholder collaboration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA wants to create a new Blueprint for an upcoming project but is unsure which tool or platform to open. Where should they navigate to create a Pega Blueprint?

options.text: pega.com/blueprint
Admin Studio
Prediction Studio
The Records tab in App Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint is accessed at a specific standalone SaaS web address (pega.com/blueprint).
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint is created and accessed at pega.com/blueprint, reflecting its standalone SaaS nature — it is not embedded in Admin Studio, Prediction Studio, or the Records tab.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A System Architect is preparing to import a Pega Blueprint into an existing application and needs to know what to expect. Which TWO statements about the Blueprint import process are correct?

options.text: A Blueprint can be imported into a new OR an existing application
All imported assets are placed in a Branch except Access Roles
Import always overwrites the entire production database
Only the BA can import a Blueprint

practiceQuiz.hint: Keep in mind that Blueprint can target new or existing apps, and Access Roles are the Branch exception.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Imports can target new or existing apps, and assets land in a Branch except Access Roles. Import does not overwrite the production database, and the LSA (not the BA) performs the import. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is presenting the Pega Blueprint workflow to new project team members who have never worked with AI-assisted design before. Which option best captures the correct end-to-end Blueprint flow?

options.text: Describe in business terms → Blueprint proposes design → refine collaboratively → export and import into Pega to jumpstart the build
Write Java → compile → deploy
Open Admin Studio → monitor system → restart
Create Access Roles → lock Rulesets → publish

practiceQuiz.hint: The Blueprint process is: describe the business → AI proposes → refine → import to jumpstart build.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Blueprint workflow is: describe the application in business terms → AI proposes the design → the team refines → export or import into Pega Platform to jumpstart development. The other options describe unrelated activities.

quickRecap.value: GenAI-infused, standalone SaaS design tool; no Pega login required to collaborate; created at pega.com/blueprint.
Augments App Studio and other tools — does not replace them; applies decades of best practices via templates.
From a business-terms description: Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas — then refined collaboratively.
Export and import into a NEW or EXISTING app; produces a functional app in minutes; performed by the LSA.
Import creates all assets in a Branch EXCEPT Access Roles.
NOT required to import a Blueprint.
Start from industry best-practice templates (e.g., Customer Service for Insurance) and refine for the organization.
